brief: Mattresses, pillows and seat cushions with a patented grid design. $1,000+ for a mattress. Back-pain sufferers and sleepers who run hot.

profile.business_summary: DTC brand selling premium mattresses, pillows, and seat cushions featuring a patented grid design, specifically targeting individuals with back pain and those who sleep hot.
stated_claims: Designed for sleepers who run hot

relevant_tags.why: Core product category for mattresses and pillows.
Mattresses and cushions are major home purchases.
The product targets physical health issues like back pain and sleep quality.
Pillows and bedding accessories fall under home textiles.

persona_conflicts.evidence: Advertiser messaging focuses strictly on functional/performance pain points like 'back-pain' and 'sleepers who run hot' rather than aesthetic appeal.

persona_conflicts.conflict: High price sensitivity and disinterest in luxury-only messaging

note_signals.why: Older affluent women with high AOV are an ideal demographic for premium back-pain relief products.
Northbed is a direct competitor in the bedding and home textiles space, meaning they will likely block this advertiser.
Science-forward wellness audience will appreciate the patented grid design and functional back-pain relief claims.
Highest-AOV apparel publisher matches the premium $1,000+ price point of the mattresses.

profile.gate_reason: The product, target audience, and price point are clearly defined, allowing for immediate campaign planning.

config.advertiser_summary: DTC brand selling premium mattresses, pillows, and seat cushions featuring a patented grid design, specifically targeting individuals with back pain and those who sleep hot.

assumptions: No target CPA/ROAS or margin given; assumed 55% gross margin (typical for home). Give a target CPA to replace this.
Target CPA = 70% of max affordable CAC ($1000 x 55% margin x 1.1 orders = $605.00).

pricing.rationale: Acquisition goal with no conversion history: pay per click. Max CPC = target CPA $423.50 x click-to-purchase rate (0.6%-2.1% for home). Clicks are observable without trusting a pixel, so both sides can verify billing.
pricing.tcpa_unlock: tCPA unlocks after conversion tracking is verified and 50 click-through conversions are recorded; until then Disco can't predict conversion rate for this brand.

budget.pacing: even daily pacing; pause a host if CPA > 2.0x target after 150 clicks

allocations.rationale: score 0.17 -> relative fit x1.40 on CTR/CVR; max bid $6.00 (break-even at target CPA), start at 70%; host also sells this kind of product: confirm it allows competing brands, otherwise this budget reflows to the other hosts
score 0.16 -> relative fit x1.35 on CTR/CVR; max bid $6.00 (break-even at target CPA), start at 70%
score 0.10 -> relative fit x1.09 on CTR/CVR; max bid $5.53 (break-even at target CPA), start at 70%

warnings: No budget given: recommending $6,190, the smallest budget that buys 300 clicks per host.

phases.name: learning
phases.rule: bid = start bid per host (70% of break-even); pacing adjustment only
phases.why: stable bids so measured CTR/CVR aren't confounded by bid changes

phases.name: enhanced_cpc
phases.until: tCPA unlocks after conversion tracking is verified and 50 click-through conversions are recorded; until then Disco can't predict conversion rate for this brand.
phases.rule: bid = start bid x conversion_likelihood x pacing, clamped to [floor, max bid]
phases.why: spend more on shoppers who look likely to buy, never above break-even

phases.name: target_cpa
phases.rule: Disco bids automatically to hit $423.50 CPA
phases.why: only once Disco can predict this brand's conversion rate

adjustments.reason: Bid higher when the shopper looks like a high converter: their persona match for this campaign vs the host's average shopper (from the serve-time persona posterior).
Under-delivering vs the daily plan -> bid up a little; over-delivering -> bid down.

bid_strategy.rationale: Start below break-even and fixed so the first two weeks measure the hosts, not the bidder; then bid per shopper within a hard ceiling (max CPC = target CPA x CVR), so a single click can never cost more than it's expected to earn.
